CHOICE: 1
CONFIDENCE: 3

Solution 1 gives $\max\{2/p,\,3-p\}$. Its heuristic holds up when checked: a spike of size $x$ dilutes in time about $x^2$ on the cycle, and a union bound over $n$ vertices gives $\mathbb P(\text{spike}>\varepsilon\sqrt t)\approx n\,t^{-p/2}$. Integrating this tail for $t\le n^2$ gives $n^{2/p}$ when $p>2$ and $n^{3-p}$ when $p<2$. Solution 2 omits the $n^{3-p}$ regime, which dominates for $1<p<2$, so it is wrong there. Solution 3 assumes bounded data and so misses the heavy-tail effect. I have not verified the matching upper bound or the literature result, so the confidence is moderate.
